claims.text: Adding approximately 2 at% Nb to a phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloy will improve its glass-forming ability.
Adding approximately 2 at% Nb will improve the thermal stability of the resulting amorphous state.
In the Nb-free baseline, amorphous-phase formation or retention is limited by crystallization during cooling or annealing.
Nb should be added during melting before rapid solidification.
The proposed benefit requires Nb to remain soluble without forming secondary crystalline phases.
The Nb addition will increase atomic-size mismatch.
The Nb addition will enhance short-range chemical order.
The Nb-induced local structural changes will disrupt crystalline nucleation sites.
The Nb-induced local structural changes will produce a more uniformly disordered melt structure that persists in the amorphous solid.
Nb has a distinct atomic size and negative mixing enthalpy with the unspecified existing alloy constituents.
Nb addition will increase the viscosity of the liquid alloy.
Nb addition will reduce atomic mobility during rapid cooling.
Reduced atomic mobility will impede the formation of crystalline nuclei during cooling.
Reduced atomic mobility will retard crystallization during subsequent annealing.
The Nb-containing alloy will remain fully amorphous over a broader range of cooling rates than the Nb-free baseline.
The Nb-containing alloy will have a higher crystallization onset temperature than the Nb-free baseline.
The Nb-containing alloy will exhibit an increased ΔTx relative to the Nb-free baseline.
Nb contents significantly above approximately 2 at% may produce secondary crystalline phases and negate the proposed benefits.
The proposed effect is expected only in alloys whose overall compositions support high atomic packing efficiency and chemical complexity.
The efficacy of Nb will depend on the full alloy composition, processing parameters, and Nb solubility in the amorphous matrix.

contradictions.description: The predicted-outcome text treats an increase in crystallization onset temperature as an increase in ΔTx, whereas the measurement plan lists crystallization onset temperature and ΔTx as separate quantities. ΔTx normally denotes a temperature interval rather than the crystallization onset temperature itself.
